record.paper_title: Some open questions in axion theory
record.original_question: What is the correct treatment of the interactions between magnetic monopoles or dyons and massless fermions, and how should those fermions be incorporated into the computation of virtual dyon loops so that the special massless-fermion limit is reproduced correctly?

evidence.quote: It still remains to be shown how to incorporate the fermions in the computation of dyonic loops, which could reproduce this special limit. One crucial first step is to understand the interactions between magnetic monopoles/dyons and massless fermions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a four-dimensional gauge theory containing magnetic monopoles (and, more generally, dyons carrying both magnetic and electric charges) coupled to massless charged Dirac fermions. In the path-integral computation of the axion potential induced by virtual monopole/dyon loops, the axion couples to the dyon collective coordinate (the periodic "dyon degree of freedom" associated with the Witten effect), and a non-trivial potential is generated by Euclidean monopole worldlines winding around this collective coordinate. It is known that this monopole-loop-generated axion potential must vanish identically in the limit in which there exists at least one massless electrically charged fermion in the spectrum.

Formulate a consistent quantum-mechanical treatment of the interactions between magnetic monopoles or dyons and massless fermions, including the correct boundary conditions and effective dynamics at the monopole core (analogous to the Callan–Rubakov problem), and incorporate these fermions explicitly into the computation of virtual dyon loops contributing to the axion potential, in such a way that the resulting axion potential vanishes in the massless-fermion limit while smoothly reproducing the known non-vanishing result when the fermions are given a mass.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works have made substantial progress on monopole/dyon–massless-fermion interactions (Callan–Rubakov effect with dyonic boundary conditions and "dyon degrees of freedom"), and on the axion potential from monopole loops including the vanishing in the massless-fermion limit. A 2024 JHEP paper proposes "a new solution to the Callan–Rubakov effect," and 2021–2025 works extend the dyon-loop computation. However, a complete, universally accepted incorporation of massless fermions into the virtual dyon-loop computation that smoothly reproduces the massless limit is still under active development, so the question is partially solved rather than definitively settled.

status_evidence.title: A new solution to the Callan Rubakov effect (JHEP 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a complete physical picture of monopole-fermion interaction, with fermions interacting with periodic scalar 'dyon degrees of freedom' localized on the monopole.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on consistent treatment of monopole/dyon interactions with fermions.

status_evidence.title: Axion Mass from Magnetic Monopole Loops (PRL 2021)
status_evidence.snippet: Axion potential from monopole loops via Witten effect; vanishes in the presence of a massless charged fermion.
status_evidence.claim: The massless-fermion limit and its effect on the dyon-loop-induced axion potential is identified, but the explicit fermion-inclusive computation remains open.

status_evidence.title: Dyon Loops and Abelian Instantons (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Further development of dyon-loop computations of axion potentials.
status_evidence.claim: Active ongoing research on dyon-loop axion potential computations.
